oneLine: Bitcoin and Ethereum declined about 2% on November 2 as traders rotated into altcoins amid lingering caution over the massive Binance breach, while funding costs remained sky-high and broad market breadth strengthened.
caveman: On Monday, Bitcoin and Ethereum each dropped about 2%, but something interesting happened: smaller cryptocurrencies actually went UP in price. People were moving their money to different coins because they were worried. The big scary thing was that hackers from North Korea had stolen billions of dollars from Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange, just a couple of days before. Even though Binance was trying to give everyone their money back, people were still nervous and scared more bad things might happen. It was a worrying day with prices down, but not as crazy as when the hack first happened.
priceVolumeSummary: All five major exchanges (Binance, Bybit, OKX, Bitget, Gate) showed nearly identical Bitcoin and Ethereum prices throughout the day, with Binance leading volume at $8.97 billion in BTC trading and $7.48 billion in ETH. Bitcoin fell 1.94% to $76,791 and Ethereum dropped 0.94% to $2,252.80.
positioningSummary: Despite the price decline, Bitcoin's open interest rose 1.93% as traders added long-side leverage—a sign of conviction to buy below $77,000. Ethereum's open interest fell 2.01% as some longs were cleared. Both assets carried extreme funding rates of 10.95% annualized, well above normal levels, signaling heavy overleveraging to the upside. Bitcoin's top traders held a 1.67× long-to-short ratio and the taker buy/sell ratio stood at 1.05, showing slight buying aggression. Remarkably, 70% of all Binance perpetuals traded higher on the day despite major coins declining—a classic sign of money rotating into smaller altcoins. The Fear & Greed index ticked up to 37 (Fear level) from 34, reflecting ongoing unease after the exchange hack.
stocksSummary: Korean semiconductor stocks led Asian markets on November 2, with SK Hynix climbing 4.0% and Samsung Electronics rising 3.6%, lifting the broader KOSPI index 2.2%. Hong Kong's chip-leverage plays mirrored the move, with a 2× SK Hynix ETF surging 7.4%. The driver of semiconductor strength on the day was not clear from available announcements.

topThree.headline: Binance's $6.3 billion hack began with fake job interviews and exploitation of internal AI tool
topThree.what: On November 3, Binance released a detailed incident report showing North Korean-linked attackers spent months compromising employee credentials via fake recruitment interviews. They then exploited a compromised internal AI tool to access the hot-wallet signing infrastructure (via Ethereum's EIP-7702 delegation mechanism), stealing over $6.3 billion in crypto. Binance said it has since replaced 90% of stolen assets.

topThree.headline: CFTC approves stock perpetual futures for US trading, bringing crypto-native products to Wall Street
topThree.what: On November 3, the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission approved equity perpetual futures on regulated US exchanges. This extends a trading product native to crypto markets—perpetuals allow leverage with no expiration and financing between long and short traders. The move gives US traders a regulated alternative to offshore venues.

topThree.headline: CZ warns of AI-driven cyberattacks, calls for industry-wide crypto security alliance
topThree.what: In his first interview since the Binance hack, Changpeng Zhao stated on November 3 that artificial intelligence is accelerating the pace and sophistication of cyberattacks across the crypto sector. He called for an industry security alliance to coordinate response and share threat intelligence, signaling that the Binance breach is likely the start of a wave of AI-powered attacks.

Regulation and policy.headline: SEC issues no-action letter for Canton Coin, calling it a digital commodity
Regulation and policy.what: The SEC's Division of Corporation Finance stated it will not recommend enforcement against Canton Coin's programmatic issuance, effectively classifying the token as a digital commodity rather than a security. The letter provides clarity on token classification.

Regulation and policy.headline: Moscow Exchange to launch Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT trading in December
Regulation and policy.what: Russia's primary exchange announced it will begin trading Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tether starting December 1 under the country's new crypto law. Non-qualified investors will face annual purchase limits.

Exchange and platform changes.headline: Amazon, Tesla, SpaceX, Netflix block their tokenized shares from OKX-ICE venue
Exchange and platform changes.what: Major tech firms including Amazon, Tesla, SpaceX, Netflix, and Lam Research filed objections blocking their stock tokens from trading on the planned OKX-ICE tokenized stock exchange. Total objections reached 56 companies—nearly 80% of the original roster—effectively dismantling the project.

Exchange and platform changes.headline: GitBook suffers AI agent security breach, urges users to rotate keys
Exchange and platform changes.what: Documentation platform GitBook reported that attackers used AI-assisted methods to gain access to infrastructure credentials. The breach prompted a shutdown and emergency token resets for users.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin pledges full refund after $40 million hack
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: Brazil's largest Bitcoin exchange announced it will refund all affected users without requiring customers to absorb the loss from a $40 million theft. Withdrawals remain frozen pending full recovery.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Chainalysis discloses AI-assisted breach exposed customer names and emails
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis reported that hackers used AI-assisted techniques to breach infrastructure and steal customer names and email addresses. The firm did not report loss of blockchain data or customer wallets.

Unconfirmed and watch items.headline: North Korea denies involvement in Binance hack
Unconfirmed and watch items.what: North Korea's state news agency (KCNA) issued an official denial of involvement in the Binance theft, despite the FBI's public attribution to North Korean state-sponsored actors. The denial came after multiple US agencies and crypto sources confirmed North Korean involvement.

Unconfirmed and watch items.headline: Tether CEO claims company holds 150,000 Bitcoin versus 100,000 in reserve reports
Unconfirmed and watch items.what: At Plan ₿ Forum in Lugano, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino stated the company owns 'give or take 150,000 Bitcoin,' but the company's Q3 reserve report implies holdings of only 100,060 BTC. The 50,000 BTC discrepancy raises questions about transparency and reserve accounting.

glossary.definition: The percentage of individual coins trading higher versus lower on the day; high breadth indicates broad-based buying across the market.
A sentiment gauge ranging from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed); values below 50 indicate market pessimism.
The periodic interest rate paid between perpetual futures traders; when high and positive, long-position holders pay short-position holders, indicating the market is overleveraged with bulls.
The proportion of traders holding bullish (long) positions versus bearish (short) positions; above 1 means more bulls than bears.
The reference price used to calculate funding payments and liquidations on perpetuals; derived from a mix of spot prices across venues.
The total number of outstanding futures contracts at an exchange, measured in either coins or dollars; rising open interest means traders are adding leverage.
The percentage increase or decrease in total outstanding futures over a trading day; indicates whether the market is becoming more or less leveraged.
When traders have borrowed more money than prudent relative to their actual assets; increases the risk of forced liquidations if prices move against them.
Futures contracts without expiration dates, allowing traders to hold leveraged positions indefinitely; prices are kept in line with spot markets via a 'funding rate' payment between longs and shorts.
The ratio of market-taking buy orders to market-taking sell orders; above 1 indicates more aggressive buying, below 1 indicates more aggressive selling.
The ratio of long to short positions held by the largest traders on an exchange; indicates directional bias of institutional money.
